How Tide Pools Survive the Summer

Every summer the rock pools along the northern shore lose most of their water to evaporation between tides, and the animals that live in them have to cope with water that grows warmer and saltier by the hour until the sea returns in the evening.

Anemones close up and hold water inside their bodies, while small crabs hide under the shaded side of stones. Researchers who measured the pools for three years found that the shaded pools stayed up to six degrees cooler than the open ones on the hottest afternoons.

The study also found that pools with more seaweed kept their oxygen levels stable for longer, because the plants kept producing oxygen in daylight, which helped the animals through the hottest part of the day.
